<entry id="M00627">
<head-word>מוֹרָה</head-word>
<hw-number>I</hw-number>
<pos> m.</pos>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (b. h.; = מערה, of Phoenician origin, v. Wellh.</definition>
<notes> Text d. B. Sam., p. 146, sq.) 
<italic>razor.</italic> Naz. IX, 5; Midr. Sam. ch. II מה מ' האמור(ה) וכ' as the word 
<italic>morah</italic> which is used in connection with Samson (Jud. XIII, 5) intimates that he shall be a nazarite, so also &c. (I Sam. I, 1</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>; v. 
<xref rid="M00628">next w.</xref>—Num. R. s. 10 why is the razor (תער) called 
<italic>morah?</italic> שאין השער מתיירא וכ' for the hair is afraid of nothing but the razor (v. מוֹרָא); v. Midr. Sam. l.</definition>
<notes> c.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="M00628">
<head-word>מוֹרָה</head-word>
<hw-number>II</hw-number>
<pos> m.</pos>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (cmp. מָרוּת) 
<italic>authority.</italic></definition>
<notes> Naz. IX, 5 והלא אין מ' אלא של בו"ד does not this 
<italic>morah</italic> (I Sam. I, 11, v. Targ.) mean, ‘the authority of man (shall not come upon his head)’? שכבר היה עליו מ' של בו"ד (Var. מורא) the authority of man was obviously upon him (I Sam. XVI, 2); Midr. Sam. ch. II (corr. acc.).</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="M00631">
<head-word>מוֹרֶה</head-word>
<hw-number>II</hw-number>
<pos> m.</pos>
<language-key>(b. h. </language-key>
<language-reference>
<xref rid="unknown">מֹרֶה; part. of מָרָה)</xref></language-reference>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>rebellious</italic>.</definition>
<notes>—
<plural-form>Pl. מוֹרִים</plural-form>. Tanḥ. Ḥuck. 9 (ref. to המרים, Num. XX, 10) מהו המ' … המ' סרבנים what does this 
<italic>hammorim</italic> mean? There are several explanations of it: 
<italic>hamm</italic>. means ‘trouble-some’; המ' שוטין וכ' 
<italic>hammorim</italic> means ‘fools’, for in the sea towns they call fools 
<italic>morim</italic> (v. מוֹרוֹס); ויש אומרים המ' שמורים את מלמדיהן and some say, 
<italic>hamm</italic>. means those who presume to teach their teachers; (or) המורים חצים וכ' those who shoot arrows (with ref. to I Sam. XXXI, 3); v. יָרָה; Num. R. s. 19.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="M00632">
<head-word>מוֹרֶה</head-word>
<hw-number>III</hw-number>
<senses>
<sense>

<italic>fool!</italic></definition>
<notes>Pesik. Shimʿu. p. 118
<sup>b</sup> למלך … אל תהי קורא לבני מ' like to a king who gave his son in charge of a pedagogue and said, never call my son fool; מה הדין לישנא מ' כהדין … מורוס what does this 
<italic>moré</italic> mean?—As in Greek they call a fool 
<italic>moros</italic>; Yalk. Jer. 265; Yalk. Num. 764 לִּבְנִי מורים … (corr. acc.).</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="M00650">

<italic>brine, pickle</italic> containing fish-hash and sometimes wine.</definition>

<sup>c</sup> bot. תומנתא עתיקתא דמ' וכ' an old Tumanta (eighth of a kab) for 
<italic>muries</italic> in Sepphoris. Y. Ter. VIII, 45
<sup>b</sup> bot., v. צִירָא I. Tosef. Ber. IV, 2. Tosef. Dem. I, 24; Ḥull. 6

<sense>

<italic>mazon</italic> (nourishment) is permitted to partake of water and salt. Ib. 30
<sup>a</sup>; Ber. 35
<sup>b</sup> מים ומלח הוא דלא איקרי מ' וכ' only water and salt are not called 
<italic>mazon</italic>, but all other food is included in 
<italic>mazon</italic>; Gen. R. s. 94, beg. Erub. VIII, 2 מ' ב' סעודות food for two meals. Ber. VIII, 8 לאחר המ' for the after-meal (dessert). Ib. מברך על המ' he says the grace after meal. Ib. 5 נר ומ' וכ' the benediction for the light, then for the meal, then for the spices &c.; Pes. 103

<sup>a</sup> bot. מ' הבנות מדבריהן the obligation to support the daughters from a man’s estate is a Rabbinical enactment; a. fr.—
<plural-form>Pl. מְזוֹנוֹת</plural-form>. Ber. 35
<sup>b</sup> בורא מיני מ' (abbrev. במ"מ) (Blessed be he) who created various kinds of food. Keth. IV, 6 חייב במ' בתו bound to support his daughter. Ib. XI, 2 אין לה מ' she cannot claim alimentation. <italic>manzil</italic> hospitium) [
<italic>station of the stars</italic>,] 
<italic>constellation of the Zodiac;</italic> in gen. 
<italic>planet</italic>. Gen. R. s. 10 יש מ' שגומר הלוכו וכ' there is a planet that finishes its circuit in thirty days …, in twelve months &c. Ib. נוגה מהלכת י"ב מזלות … מ' וכ' the Venus passes the twelve constellations in ten months, requiring for each station twenty five days; a. fr.—
<plural-form>Pl. מַזָּלוֹת</plural-form>. Ib. Ber. 32
<sup>b</sup> שנים עשר מ' וכ' I have created twelve stations in the heavens, and for each station I have appointed thirty legions (of stars), v. גַּסְטְרָא. Tosef. ib. VII (VI), 6 הרואה … ואת המ' [כסדרן] he who sees the sun, the moon and the stars and planets in their original position (at the end of a lunisolar period). Sabb. 75
<sup>a</sup> חישוב תקופות ומ' the calculation of periods and constellations. Gen. R. s. 25; Y. Pes. I, 27
<sup>b</sup> top לא שמשו המ' וכ' the planets did no service during the year of the flood; a. fr.—עובד כוכבום ומ' (abbrev. עכו"ם) 
<italic>idolater</italic>, v. עָבַד, a. עֲבוֹדָה.—Trnsf. (astrology) 
<italic>constellation at one’s birth, planet, destiny; guardian angel, angel of destiny</italic>. Gen. R. s. 10 אין לך כל עשב … שאין לו מ' וכ' there is not an herb which has not a planet in heaven that strikes it and says, Grow!—Sabb. 156
<sup>a</sup> לא מַזַּל יום גורם מ' שעה וכ' not the day’s planet, but the constellation of the hour (of birth) has influence. Ib. מ' מחכים וכ' the planet (of birth) makes wise, rich &c. Ib. אין מ' לישראל Israel is not dependent on nativity; a. v. fr.</notes></sense></senses></entry>
